chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The person in Ihram slaughters (the animal they are required to offer) what is permissible for the one in a state of normalcy (Halal) in the Sanctuary (Haram), meaning that he slaughters it himself in both the Sanctuary and the open land (Hill).

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.لِلْحَلَالِ: For the permissible (one in normal state)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the animal slaughtered by a pilgrim in Ihram regarding its permissibility and location of slaughter?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific type of animal required for the expiation (kaffarah) of a pilgrim who slaughters game, mandating that it be a common, permissible animal (halal) rather than a specialized sacrificial offering. It establishes the principle that the pilgrim personally performs the slaughter, ensuring the validity of the act within both the sacred precincts (Haram) and the broader sanctuary (Hill). This ruling underscores the continuity of Ihram restrictions on hunting even during the act of expiation.
